text:
rae.ops: Heads up — after today's 12:00 deploy we’re seeing a 15–30ms tail latency increase on SSE streams specifically hitting tool-calling codepaths. P50 looks fine, but p95/p99 moved. Rolling back on standby. cc @vikram @jun

vikram: Saw the same on the perf dashboard (grafana link). Spike aligns exactly with the merge for PR #489. Traces point to more time spent in the streaming encoder / serialization.

ci-bot: perf-run: http://ci.local/perf/1943 — baseline vs head attached. Quick summary: flamegraph shows increased stack in stream_encoder::encode_frame and memcpy-heavy work.

jun: I can bisect this. Steps I’m running:
```
git fetch origin
git checkout release
git bisect start --good v1.19.0 --bad HEAD
# run bench script (local)
./tools/bench_stream_latency.sh --runs 5 --warmup 10
```
If someone else is on it, shout now.

sara: Ran a quick pprof on staging (after reproducing the spike): top nodes are encode_frame -> write_sse -> kv_cache::get. KV cache miss rate is ~2x higher in the bad build. Hypothesis: framing change altered cache keys and also increased per-frame bytes causing more memcpy.

vikram: That matches my read. PR 489 made two related changes: added extra tool metadata into event headers and consolidated encode paths which removed our zero-copy fastpath. Small diff snippet from the merge: 
```diff
-// zero-copy path: reference buffer, write out fragment
-void serialize_frame(BufferRef ref) { /* single ref */ }
+// unified path: copy into contiguous buffer for safety
+void serialize_frame(BufferRef ref) {
+  auto tmp = malloc(ref.size);
+  memcpy(tmp, ref.ptr, ref.size);
+  write(tmp, ref.size);
+}
```
That memcpy shows up in the flamegraphs. Also the header bytes changed which looks to affect kvcache keys if the key used the full serialized header.

jun: Removing zero-copy would explain both extra CPU and allocations. If the cache key salts on serialized header length or a non-stable field, any header schema change will churn entries. Do we have tests covering kv-cache key stability across framing changes?

rae.ops: Two paths: revert PR 489 (fast) or re-enable zero-copy behind an env var/feature flag (slower but safer to keep framing changes). Which do we prefer for a hotfix?

vikram: Revert is fastest to get latency back. I’ve opened a revert PR (r/501) and started a canary deploy (10% traffic). I'll post canary perf after one full hour.

sara: While revert proceeds, I can prepare a minimal mitigation: normalizing the header fields used for the kvcache key (strip non-stable tool metadata) — small patch with low risk. I'll open a PR and we can land if revert takes longer.

jun: Quick bisect result for the record: bisect identified commit abcd123 (merge of PR 489) as first bad. Local bench numbers: p50 ~= baseline, p95 +28ms, cpu sys% +12. Attached short perf flamegraph png to the pipeline artifact.

ci-bot: CI perf job flagged regression on release branch: perf/stream-latency #236 failed (threshold exceeded). Logs and flamegraphs are attached to the job.

rae.ops: Revert r/501 merged to release and promoted to canary. Early canary numbers show tail latencies returned to baseline. Monitoring for 30m. :thumbsup:

vikram: Follow-ups I’m creating: (1) unit test for kvcache key stability when headers evolve, (2) integration perf test for streaming encoder under tool headers, (3) design doc on safe zero-copy reintroduction with ownership guarantees. Filing now.

sara: Filed infra tickets: ENG-ppo-332 (kvcache-key-stability) and ENG-ppo-333 (stream-encoder-perf-tests). Uploaded annotated flamegraphs and pprof snapshots to the ticket.

jun: Thanks all. Postmortem next if we see any SLA blips. Also want to do a deeper code review to see why zero-copy was removed — looks like a safety concern in the merge notes; maybe solvable with reference counting / slice semantics.

rae.ops: Agree. Keep this thread updated if any canary anomalies. Closing here once release monitoring window is green.

(automated) deploy-bot: Canary 10% -> 100% promoted: no regressions observed in final window.
